purpose: Historical reconstruction hardware mapping only. This file does not contain historical prices and does not change the current headline models.
benchmarkBasis: Exact cloud VM shape; measurements were made after the historical price dates. The scores are retrospectively frozen hardware descriptors, not contemporary observations in each year.
matchingPolicy: Match historical AWS instanceType exactly, then require historical vCPU and memory specifications to agree with this mapping. Retain only records actually priced and available in the historical archive. Do not infer availability from present-day shape names.
limitations: Geekbench 6 was released on 2023-02-14. Pre-2023 benchmark-normalized values necessarily reconstruct history using later measurements.

A VM shape can have hardware, firmware, hypervisor, operating-system, or security-mitigation changes over its lifetime; matching the same name and nominal specifications does not prove its historical performance equaled the later score.
The sample includes only shapes with surviving/current matching public benchmark measurements and is subject to survivor and coverage bias. It is not a historical cross-provider market index.
The historical GPU cohort requires CPU Geekbench, RAM, whole GPU count, and GPU memory bandwidth. FP32, VRAM, and GPU Geekbench are not regression inputs, and are not required for inclusion.
The reference CPU host of 16 GiB RAM and Geekbench 6 multi-core score 20000 is a hypothetical model query outside the joint support of current eligible hardware; early years extrapolate even farther.
P2 contributes only one GPU family in 2016. A one-parameter GPU coefficient can be estimated but independent generalization cannot be established from that single family.
